gist: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a Your First Home scheme for first-time buyers.
The initiative offers 20 per cent equity loans for buyers with small deposits.
Conservatives warned the policy could increase buyer debt and drive up house prices.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced the Your First Home scheme to assist first-time buyers in England. The initiative offers a 20 per cent equity loan for new-build properties to buyers providing a 2.5 per cent deposit. Income, deposit, and property price caps will apply. Additionally, the government announced plans to make it easier for local councils to take over long-term empty homes and convert them into housing.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Supporters argue the policy helps young buyers lacking family financial support, while giving housebuilders confidence to build. However, Conservative critics warn that the scheme risks driving up property prices and increasing buyer debt burdens. Reports differ on announcement details: one outlet notes John Healey will formally announce the programme in the budget, while another attributes housing policy unveils to Angela Rayner.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Further details on how the equity loan scheme operates are expected in the upcoming Budget, with registration targeted to open by the end of 2026.

gist: US death row inmate Christa Pike is unconscious after a failed lethal injection execution.
Lawyers claim prison officials botched the execution by failing to insert IV lines correctly.
Tennessee's governor ordered an independent review and halted all executions for the year.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: US death row inmate Christa Pike is unconscious and on a ventilator following a failed execution attempt. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion to preserve evidence, alleging prison officials botched the lethal injection. They state officials used at least seven needles, bending one, while Pike whimpered and cried. An expert suggested the drug pentobarbital entered tissue under her skin rather than her bloodstream due to ruptured veins or blood clots.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has halted all executions in the state for the year and ordered an independent review. Pike's lawyers had previously warned that her blood-clotting condition and small veins risked causing unnecessary pain.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Authorities have not yet said whether they will attempt to execute Pike again, and her lawyers are seeking to preserve all physical, written, and electronic evidence.

gist: Broadcaster and campaigner Dame Esther Rantzen has died at the age of 86.
She was famous for presenting That's Life! and founding the charity Childline.
In her later years, she campaigned to change laws around assisted dying.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Broadcaster and campaigner Dame Esther Rantzen has died aged 86. Her family confirmed her death, paying tribute to her legacy of compassion. Rantzen, who was diagnosed with stage four lung cancer in 2023, became a prominent campaigner for assisted dying. She had planned to end her life at the Swiss clinic Dignitas but became too physically frail to make the journey.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rantzen was a pioneering television presenter, hosting the BBC's popular consumer show That's Life! for 21 years. She used her platform to launch Childline in 1986, a helpline for children experiencing abuse. In 2010, she established the Silver Line to support older people. Her campaigning work earned her a damehood and praise from Prime Minister Andy Burnham for giving a voice to the unheard.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A new wave of heavy rain and landslides has killed about 30 people in Nepal. Over 1,900 families have been affected, with homes, roads and bridges damaged or swept away. Hundreds of trekkers on the Annapurna Circuit have cut short their hikes, with many helicoptered out of Manang and Mustang districts. An avalanche near Himlung Peak left four dead and 12 missing.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The disaster follows August's catastrophic flooding that left 1,400 dead and thousands missing. Communities are left homeless, staying in leaking tents and mourning relatives. The Annapurna Circuit, which is crucial to Nepal's economy, has faced severe transport and communication disruptions, stranding visitors and preventing hundreds more from starting.

gist: California has banned child marriage, becoming the 18th US state to outlaw the practice.

Survivors and campaigners pledged to continue fighting until child marriage ends in all states.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Governor Gavin Newsom signed Assembly bill 1267, prohibiting minors from receiving a marriage licence or entering a domestic partnership. The law contains no exceptions. Previously, children of any age could marry with parental consent and judicial approval.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: California is the 18th state to ban child marriage since 2018, leaving it legal in 32 states. The advocacy group Unchained At Last reported that about 9,000 children—predominantly girls—were wed annually in California, mostly to adult men. Survivors highlighted that minors could not legally divorce, leaving them vulnerable to abuse.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: A survivor noted that minors cannot marry in California after 1 January 2027. Activists, including survivor Courtney Stodden, pledged to continue campaigning until child marriage is banned across all 50 US states.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In December 2022, a man obtained a key to a guest's room at a Maidenhead Travelodge and sexually assaulted her. An independent review by Paul Greaney KC found the chain failed the victim "at every stage", including offering her an "insulting" £30 refund.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The review found Travelodge's security policies were unfit for purpose. Despite recent changes, guests remain at risk, with room intrusions reported at nearly one in ten Travelodge hotels this summer.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Travelodge has apologised and established a board committee to implement the review's 38 recommendations. These include introducing staff body cameras, consistent CCTV, and stricter key security checks.

fivew: An independent review led by barrister Paul Greaney KC.

Kyiv argues it must target infrastructure while Russia bombards Ukrainian cities.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Ukraine struck an oil facility in Russia’s Samara region, a Russian vessel in the Black Sea, and a drone site in Oryol. Donald Trump urged Volodymyr Zelenskyy to halt refinery attacks, blaming them for global diesel shortages and rising US fuel prices.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The attacks have knocked out over 45% of Russia’s refining capacity. However, they also tighten global diesel supplies and increase cost of living pressures in the US ahead of midterm elections, though analysts cite other market disruptions too.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Kyiv is unlikely to stop targeting Russian oil infrastructure while Moscow continues its daily attacks. Russia has extended its diesel export ban until the end of October.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Chief Constable Jon Boutcher announced that the Drumcree parading dispute's policing operation has cost about £3m. The stand-off began on Sunday over a proposed Orange Order parade in Portadown, opposed by Garvaghy Road nationalist residents. Although the Parades Commission ruled the march could lawfully proceed, police have not forced it through due to an unlawful protest.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Boutcher warned that forcing the march could have "catastrophic" consequences. The Drumcree dispute, which began in the mid-1990s, previously caused severe violence, nearly derailing the peace process. Additionally, the Policing Board is investigating member Deirdre Hargey of Sinn Féin after she was pictured at the protest.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Boutcher is allowing space for negotiations. A thorough police investigation into the protest is underway, and a fresh legal challenge by the Garvaghy Road Residents Coalition will be heard on Friday.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The annual Orionid meteor shower has become active, with the display set to peak overnight between 21 and 22 October. The meteors are fast-moving debris left behind by Halley's Comet.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The shower offers skywatchers a chance to see up to 20 meteors per hour under ideal conditions. Because they enter the atmosphere at 41 miles per second, they can leave brief, glowing trails.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Although the shower is active until 7 November, a bright moon building towards its full phase may obscure fainter meteors during the peak. Observers are advised to seek dark locations away from streetlights, allowing their eyes to adjust, with the best viewing window potentially occurring just before dawn after moonset.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: US District Judge Amit Mehta dismissed antitrust lawsuits against Google brought by Chegg and Penske Media Corporation. The publishers accused Google of abusing monopoly power by using their content in AI Overviews without sending search traffic, hurting revenue. Mehta ruled that an expectation of search traffic does not constitute a legal agreement.

gist: Lyft agreed to pay California $272.5m to settle a driver misclassification lawsuit.
The settlement covers claims that Lyft stole drivers' wages by labelling them independent contractors.
Over $237m of the settlement will be distributed to thousands of Lyft drivers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Lyft agreed to pay California $272.5m to settle claims of wage theft from April 2016 to December 2020. The state alleged Lyft mislabelled drivers as independent contractors instead of employees. Lyft maintains drivers were properly classified.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: This is California's largest-ever wage theft settlement. It covers a period before Proposition 22 exempted ride-share drivers from state employment laws. While officials called it a landmark win, critic Veena Dubal argued the sum is paltry compared to what drivers are actually owed.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The settlement awaits court approval, after which over $237m will go to drivers. Meanwhile, a similar lawsuit against Uber continues in California.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The US supreme court agreed to hear a challenge to the Trump administration's practice of indefinite detention for undocumented immigrants awaiting deportation. The administration reinterpreted a longstanding policy last year, denying bond hearings to migrants who entered the country illegally. The challenge was brought by Ricardo Aparecido Barbosa da Cunha, a Brazilian citizen living in the US who was denied a bond hearing after being arrested by ICE agents.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The case centers on a policy reinterpretation that led to a massive surge in migrants held in detention facilities. Lower courts have been split on the issue, with most federal appeals and district court judges rejecting the administration's interpretation of the statute.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The supreme court will intervene and hear arguments in the case after lower courts ordered the government to provide a bond hearing.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The historic Palm Houses at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh have reopened after extensive restoration. Outlets disagree on the closure length, stating five or six years. More than 600 temperate plants were returned to the renovated space, which features upgraded glass panels and repaired ironwork. One Sabal palm tree over 200 years old was cut down due to its size, but a seedling descendant was planted in its place.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The glasshouses protect rare and endangered species, some of which are extinct in the wild or hold medicinal properties for human health. Severe Scottish winter weather and falling glass previously threatened the survival of these valuable plants.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: While the main palm houses are now restored, other glasshouses at the garden still await necessary upgrades to prevent ongoing weather damage to plant collections.

quotes.text: We've done really well.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Washington DC implemented a new law that prevents landlords from restricting tenants' dogs by breed, size, or weight. This measure forms the final portion of Roscoe's Law, introduced by Robert White. Earlier parts of the legislation limited pet security deposits to 15 percent of monthly rent and capped pet rent at 1 percent, while banning other non-refundable charges.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Animal welfare groups supported the measure, stating that previous restrictions made housing harder to find and unfairly punished responsible owners. Meanwhile, the DC Landlord Association voiced worries that fee limits might fail to cover property damage caused by pets.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Breed and weight rules are banned in residential leases signed after October 1, 2026. However, property websites still displayed weight limits and pet restrictions shortly after the law took effect.

His story highlights the challenges and funding issues faced by students with special educational needs.

sections.text: Patrick McCabe used eye-tracking technology to complete his GCSE exams over four months. Despite facing exhaustion and communication barriers, he passed all seven exams and started studying for his A-levels in French, business, and media studies at Fallibroome Academy.

sections.text: Patrick's success highlights the potential of inclusive education, but also exposes significant hurdles. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Apple announced plans to alter macOS privacy settings, requiring very explicit user action before apps gain full-disk access. timeline.text: Research roundup: 6 cool science stories we almost missed

gist: Researchers detected a tantalizing hint of dark matter using the LUX-ZEPLIN detector.
Physicists observed quantum entanglement in pairs of Z bosons at the Large Hadron Collider.
Engineers created a Martian building material from rocks, gelatin, and yeast.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Scientists reported several recent discoveries, including a possible dark matter signal at the LUX-ZEPLIN detector in South Dakota and quantum entanglement in Z bosons at the Large Hadron Collider. Additionally, engineers developed a living 3D-printable building material for Mars using yeast and gelatin, archaeologists found evidence of Ice Age humans chewing betel nuts 25,000 years ago in Indonesia, and a historian uncovered a 1666 description of a telescope attributed to Galileo. Finally, research revealed that 19th-century cosmoramas were used to market real estate.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: These findings advance several fields. The dark matter signal, if confirmed, could help physicists understand the universe, while observing high-energy entanglement aids quantum research. The yeast mixture offers a cost-effective, low-energy housing solution for colonizing Mars. The dental evidence provides insight into early human habits and health, and the historical texts shed new light on Galileo's scientific instruments and early real estate marketing methods.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Jim McCahy died at the age of 89. Born in Barnet and raised partly near the Tyne, he began his career in libraries before overcoming tuberculosis. After training as a teacher, he taught on Merseyside from 1961 and became headteacher of Archbishop Whiteside in 1975. He later received a council dismissal letter during the mid-1980s turmoil, managed locations of Our Lady of Fatima school, and took early retirement in 1989. In retirement, he volunteered, worked for the Council for the Protection of Rural England, appeared as a TV extra, and enjoyed various hobbies before moving to Woking in 2019.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: His life reflected significant mid-to-late 20th-century urban and educational shifts, particularly in Liverpool during a period of intense political and economic change under Margaret Thatcher's government.

sections.text: HBO Max has released Get Jiro, an adult animated series based on a graphic novel co-written by Anthony Bourdain and Joel Rose. Set in a dystopian near-future Los Angeles, the story follows Jiro, a taciturn sushi chef who decapitates a customer for dipping fish in soy sauce. In this world, virtual reality satisfies all human desires except food, making master chefs powerful crime lords.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The series satirises modern foodie culture, where restaurant criticism and ingredient provenance are treated with extreme seriousness. It uses cartoonish, gory violence to critique how food becomes class currency and a weapon. The show blends a love of food with pulp action, reflecting Bourdain's interest in kitchen energy and social politics.

timeline.text: London Labour council warns it may raise council tax by 150%

gist: Hammersmith and Fulham council warns of a potential 150% council tax increase.
The rise is blamed on central government cutting funding to wealthier areas.
The council faces its biggest financial challenge in living memory due to cuts.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Hammersmith and Fulham council warned it might increase council tax by up to 150%. This potential rise is intended to maintain services after central government funding cuts. Under a new Whitehall funding formula, the west London authority expects its government grant to be cut by more than half over four years, falling from £150.5m to £72.4m.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The government's "fair funding" review aims to redirect money to poorer areas. However, local leaders argue the formula uses flawed measures that ignore deprivation in London. Hammersmith and Fulham, which has kept bills low, says it faces its most severe financial challenge in living memory. Other London councils also face significant funding reductions.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The council's cabinet will publish a report detailing various tax rise scenarios. A 150% increase would cost Band D households an extra £29.11 weekly by 2027/28 to balance the budget. The council has been granted powers to exceed the usual 5% cap next year.

gist: BT is accused of bullying customers by temporarily pausing broadband to prompt digital upgrades.
Around 1.3 million copper landlines still need migrating before the upcoming January deadline.
Campaigners fear vulnerable and elderly people could lose vital services during the switchover.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: BT temporarily paused broadband services for a small group of unresponsive customers to encourage them to switch from copper landlines to digital services. The campaign group Silver Voices accused BT of "bullying behaviour" for threatening to cut off internet access. BT stated the temporary pause aimed to prevent a complete loss of service when the old network retires.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: About 1.3 million copper-based landlines still need migrating. Campaigners worry that vulnerable people, including the elderly and those in rural areas, could lose access to emergency services or telecare alarms. In December, Virgin Media was fined £23.8m for leaving vulnerable customers without alarm access during its transition.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Telecoms companies are racing to migrate remaining customers before the end-of-January deadline. Age UK has urged providers to ensure no older person is cut off.

sections.text: During a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying over 170 people, a co-pilot attacked Capt Smit Machchhar with a crash axe. Capt Machchhar was hospitalised in Abu Dhabi in a stable condition.

sections.text: Polymarket has allowed users to place $77,507 worth of bets on whether major global banks, including HSBC and Lloyds, will fail by the end of this year. Although UK, US, Canada, and EU residents are banned from the platform, offshore users can still participate.

sections.text: Critics warn these bets could trigger social media-fuelled bank runs or encourage market manipulation. gist: Author Min Jin Lee is releasing her third novel, focusing on Korean education and diaspora.
Lee began writing after a health diagnosis made her fear she would die young.
Her upcoming book is part of a planned four-novel series about the Korean diaspora.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Author Min Jin Lee is publishing her third novel, American Hagwon, which explores the Korean diaspora and the intense culture of private cram schools. Lee, who left her career as a corporate lawyer in 1995 following a serious health diagnosis, has spent decades writing epic novels that bring immigrant experiences to the mainstream.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Lee's previous bestseller, Pachinko, sold over five million copies globally and was adapted for television. Her work, alongside fellow writers like Nobel laureate Han Kang, highlights overlooked periods of Korean history. Lee's sprawling novels challenge the "tiger mom" stereotype and examine the true costs of elite education systems.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Now healthy thanks to experimental drugs, the 57-year-old author plans to write a fourth novel, titled Marshall Plan, focusing on Korean miners and nurses sent to West Germany in 1963.

quotes.text: In my pages, I want to be the centre
History has failed us, but no matter

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Metropolitan Police urged organisers of a pro-Palestinian student march planned for the third anniversary of the 7 October attacks to move the event. Police said they have been unable to identify the organisers.

gist: A new competitive Latino film festival is under way across venues in London.
The five-day event aims to celebrate and give voice to British-Latino identity.
Founded by Ketty Rodriguez, the festival showcases sixty films from twenty-seven countries.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A five-day competitive Latino film festival has launched in London, showcasing 60 films from 27 countries. Founded by Cuban actress Ketty Rodriguez and dancer Javier Torres, the event features features, documentaries, animation, and shorts.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rodriguez created the festival to address a lack of Latin representation in London. Filmmakers like Victor Rios highlight that the event celebrates British-Latino identity, helping the community feel heard and established within British society.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The festival, which is backed by the BFI and the City of London Corporation, runs until Tuesday.

Which clubs did Man City's 'inflated' money flow to in transfer market?

gist: Manchester City's spending changed the football transfer market, raising prices globally.
Many clubs receiving money from City struggled to spend it effectively.
Some clubs not dealing with City directly also felt financial impacts via sell-on clauses.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester City paid high fees and wages, shifting the transfer market. Clubs receiving large sums often struggled. Wolfsburg dropped in the Bundesliga after selling Kevin de Bruyne, and Monaco nearly faced relegation after selling Benjamin Mendy and Bernardo Silva. Arsenal did not challenge for the title during the period they sold four players to City. Meanwhile, ancillary fees from sell-on clauses benefited teams like Queens Park Rangers, Barnsley, and Wolves.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The influx of money was no guarantee of success, and rising prices affected others in the football economy. Clubs receiving cash sometimes floundered, while rivals not receiving funds may have been compromised.

fivew: Manchester City and multiple other football clubs.
Manchester City's spending impacted the transfer market and the fortunes of various football clubs.
Higher transfer fees and wages altered the wider football economy and club finances.

gist: John McGinn is set to earn his 92nd cap for Scotland in Skopje.
The midfielder admits his international form has recently declined and he is not undroppable.
Despite recent struggles, McGinn remains a highly cherished figure for Scotland and Aston Villa.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Scotland midfielder John McGinn is preparing to win his 92nd cap in Skopje, North Macedonia. However, his usually talismanic form for his country has recently declined, with fewer game-defining moments and a long goal drought before a recent strike against Haiti.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: McGinn is one of Scotland's most cherished players, sitting fifth in the all-time scoring chart. Despite his legendary status at club level with Aston Villa, he has faced questions over his recent international performances and insists he is not undroppable.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: McGinn hopes to recapture his best form during the match in Skopje. He is aiming to eventually reach 100 caps, following teammate Andy Robertson who achieves the milestone this weekend.

fivew: John McGinn is facing scrutiny over his recent international form ahead of his 92nd cap.

Uncapped pair James Coles and Henry Crocombe are included.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Mason Crane has been recalled for England's upcoming one-day international tri-series in Pakistan. Sam Curran and Adil Rashid return from injuries, while uncapped players James Coles and Henry Crocombe join the squad. Jofra Archer is rested, and Jos Buttler misses out due to a hamstring injury.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The series forms part of England's white-ball schedule as they build up to the 50-over World Cup. Crane also has an opportunity to push his case to be England's number one spinner in Test cricket.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: England will play in the tri-series in Pakistan, which also involves Sri Lanka, ahead of further fixtures in Australia and South Africa.
